Main.sentence: The Gulf of Mexico ( ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language)___ : Golfo de México ) is an ___E:oceanic basin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_basin)___ and a ___E:marginal sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marginal_sea)___ of the Atlantic Ocean,   mostly surrounded by the North American continent.

It is bounded on the northeast, north, and northwest by the ___E:Gulf Coast of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_of_the_United_States)___ ; on the southwest and south by the ___E:Mexican states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_states)___ of ___E:Tamaulipas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamaulipas)___ , ___E:Veracruz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veracruz)___ , ___E:Tabasco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabasco)___ , ___E:Campeche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeche)___ , ___E:Yucatán U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n)___ , and ___E:Quintana Roo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quintana_Roo)___ ; and on the southeast by ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ .

The coastal areas along the ___E:Southern U.S. states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_U.S._states)___ of ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ , ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ , ___E:Mississippi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi)___ , ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ , and Florida, which border the Gulf on the north, are occasionally referred to as the " ___E:Third Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Coast)___ " of the United States (in addition to its Atlantic and Pacific coasts), but more often as "the Gulf Coast".
The Gulf of Mexico took shape about 300 million years ago (mya) as a result of ___E:plate tectonics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plate_tectonics)___ .

The ___E:Gulf of Mexico basin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico_basin)___ is roughly oval and is about 810 ___E:nautical miles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile)___ (1,500 kilometres; 930 miles) wide. Its floor consists of ___E:sedimentary rocks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock)___ and recent sediments.

It is connected to part of the Atlantic Ocean through the ___E:Straits of Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straits_of_Florida)___ between the U.S. and Cuba, and with the ___E:Caribbean Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea)___ via the ___E:Yucatán Channel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Channel)___ between Mexico and Cuba. Because of its narrow connection to the Atlantic Ocean, the gulf has very small ___E:tidal ranges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tides)___ .
The size of the gulf basin is about 1.6 million square kilometres (620,000 square miles).
Almost half of the basin consists of shallow ___E:continental shelf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf)___ waters.
The volume of water in the basin is roughly 2.4 million cubic kilometres (580 thousand cubic miles).

The gulf is one of the most important ___E:offshore petroleum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_drilling)___ production regions in the world, making up 14% of the United States' total production.
Moisture from the Gulf of Mexico also contributes to weather across the United States, including severe weather in ___E:Tornado Alley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_Alley)___ .

As with the ___E:name of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_of_Mexico)___ , the gulf's name is associated with the ethnonym Mexica , which refers to the ___E:Nahuatl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuatl)___ -speaking people of the ___E:Valley of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valley_of_Mexico)___ better known as the ___E:Aztecs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aztecs)___ .

In ___E:Aztec religion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aztec_religion)___ , the gulf was called Chalchiuhtlicueyecatl , or 'House of ___E:Chalchiuhtlicue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalchiuhtlicue)___ ', after the deity of the seas.  Believing that the sea and sky merged beyond the horizon, they called the seas ilhuicaatl , meaning 'sky water', contrasting them with finite, landlocked bodies of water, such as lakes.

The ___E:Maya civilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_civilization)___ , which used the gulf as ___E:a major trade route U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_trade_in_the_Maya_civilization)___ , likely called the gulf nahá , meaning 'great water'.

Up to 1530, European maps depicted the gulf, though left it unlabeled.  ___E:Hernán Cortés U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Cort%C3%A9s)___ called it "Sea of the North" ( ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language)___ : Mar del Norte ) in his dispatches, while other Spanish explorers called it the "Gulf of Florida" ( Golfo de Florida ) or "Gulf of Cortés" ( Golfo de Cortés ).
A 1584 map by ___E:Abraham Ortelius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Ortelius)___ also labeled it as the "Sea of the North" ( Mare de Nort ).

Other early European maps called it the "Gulf of St. Michael" ( ___E:Latin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language)___ : Sinus S. Michaelis ),  "Gulf of ___E:Yucatán U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Peninsula)___ " ( Golfo de Iucatan ),  "Yucatán Sea" ( Mare Iuchatanicum ),  "Great ___E:Antillean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antilles)___ Gulf" ( Sinus Magnus Antillarum ), " ___E:Cathayan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathay)___ Sea" ( Mare Cathaynum ), or "Gulf of New Spain" ( ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language)___ : Golfo de Nueva España ).

At one point, ___E:New Spain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Spain)___ encircled the gulf, with the ___E:Spanish Main U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Main)___ extending into what later became Mexico and the southeastern United States.

The name "Gulf of Mexico" ( ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language)___ : golfo de México ; ___E:French U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language)___ : golphe du Mexique , later golfe du Mexique ) first appeared on a world map in 1550 and a historical account in 1552.  As with other large bodies of water, Europeans named the gulf after Mexico, land of the Mexica, because mariners needed to cross the gulf to reach that destination.

This name has been the most common name since the mid-17th century,    when it was still considered a Spanish sea.  French ___E:Jesuits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuits)___ used this name as early as 1672.  In the 18th century, Spanish admiralty charts similarly labeled the gulf as "Mexican Cove" or "Mexican Sound" ( Ensenada Mexicana or Seno Mexicano ).

Until the ___E:Republic of Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Texas)___ broke away from Mexico in 1836, Mexico's coastal boundary extended eastward along the gulf to present-day Louisiana.

Among the other ___E:languages of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Mexico)___ , the gulf is known as Ayollohco Mexihco in ___E:Nahuatl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuatl)___ , u golfoil México in ___E:Yucatec Maya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucatec_Maya_language)___ , and golfo yu'un México in ___E:Tzotzil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tzotzil_language)___ .

Although there is no formal protocol on the general naming of ___E:international waters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_waters)___ , Gulf of Mexico is officially recognized by the ___E:International Hydrographic Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Hydrographic_Organization)___ ,   which seeks to standardize the names of international maritime features for certain purposes  and counts all three countries adjacent to the gulf as member states.

In ___E:a January 2025 executive order U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Order_14172)___ , United States president ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ directed ___E:federal agencies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_agencies_in_the_United_States)___ to adopt the name Gulf of America for the waters bounded by the U.S.    [b] While major online map platforms and several U.S.-based media outlets voluntarily adopted the change,    ___E:controversy over the name U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico_naming_controversy)___ included Mexican president ___E:Claudia Sheinbaum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudia_Sheinbaum)___ objecting to the declaration.

The ___E:International Hydrographic Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Hydrographic_Organization)___ publication Limits of Oceans and Seas [c] defines the southeast limit of the Gulf of Mexico as:

A line joining ___E:Cape Catoche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Catoche)___ ___E:Light U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_lighthouses_in_Mexico)___ ( 21°37′N 87°04′W﻿ / ﻿21.617°N 87.067°W﻿ / 21.617; -87.067 ) with the ___E:Light U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabo_San_Antonio_Lighthouse)___ on ___E:Cape San Antonio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_San_Antonio,_Cuba)___ in Cuba, through this island to the ___E:meridian of 83°W U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/83rd_meridian_west)___ and to the Northward along this meridian to the latitude of the South point of the ___E:Dry Tortugas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_Tortugas)___ (24°35′N), along this parallel Eastward to ___E:Rebecca Shoal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Shoal_Light)___ (82°35′W) thence through the shoals and ___E:Florida Keys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Keys)___ to the mainland at the eastern end of ___E:Florida Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Bay)___ and all the narrow waters between the ___E:Dry Tortugas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_Tortugas_National_Park)___ and the mainland being considered to be within the Gulf.
The total population of the five U.S. states facing the gulf is 67 million people.

Of these, a total of 15.8 million people live in the Gulf Coastal Region, in counties directly bordering the gulf.  [full citation needed] The six Mexican states that face the gulf have a total population of 19.1 million people.  [full citation needed] Three provinces of northwest ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ , including ___E:Havana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana)___ , border on the gulf, with a combined population of 3,211,000.

By 1975, 400 offshore ___E:drilling rigs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drilling_rig)___ in the gulf hosted a temporary population of more than 10,000 workers on any given day, who were rotated on a weekly staggered schedule.
Increasing automation later led to a decline in the offshore worker population.
The consensus among geologists    is that before the late ___E:Triassic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triassic)___ , the Gulf of Mexico did not exist.

Before the late Triassic, the area consisted of dry land, which included ___E:continental crust U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_crust)___ that now underlies ___E:Yucatán U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n)___ , within the middle of the supercontinent ___E:Pangaea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangaea)___ .

This land lay south of a continuous mountain range that extended from north-central Mexico, through the ___E:Marathon Uplift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Uplift)___ in west ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ and the ___E:Ouachita Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ouachita_Mountains)___ of ___E:Oklahoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma)___ , and to ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ where it linked directly to the ___E:Appalachian Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Mountains)___ .
It was created by the collision of continental plates that formed Pangaea.

As interpreted by Roy Van Arsdale and Randel T. Cox, this mountain range was breached in the late ___E:Cretaceous U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous)___ by the formation of the ___E:Mississippi Embayment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Embayment)___ .

The ___E:rifting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift)___ that created the basin was associated with zones of weakness within Pangaea, including ___E:sutures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suture_(geology))___ where the ___E:Laurentia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurentia)___ , ___E:South American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_American_Plate)___ , and ___E:African U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Plate)___ plates collided to create it. First, there was a late Triassic–early ___E:Jurassic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic)___ phase of rifting during which ___E:rift valleys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_valley)___ formed and filled with continental ___E:red beds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_beds)___ .
Second, the continental crust was stretched and thinned as rifting progressed through early and middle Jurassic times.

This thinning created a broad zone of transitional crust, which displays modest and uneven thinning with ___E:block faulting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fault_block)___ and a broad zone of uniformly thinned transitional crust, which is half the typical 40 km (25-mile) thickness of continental crust.
At this time, rifting first created a connection to the Pacific Ocean across central Mexico and later eastwards to the Atlantic Ocean.

This flooded the opening basin to create an enclosed marginal sea. The subsiding transitional crust was blanketed by the widespread deposition of ___E:Louann Salt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louann_Salt)___ and associated ___E:anhydrite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhydrite)___ ___E:evaporites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaporite)___ .

During the late Jurassic, continued rifting widened the basin and progressed to the point that ___E:seafloor spreading U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seafloor_spreading)___ and formation of ___E:oceanic crust U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_crust)___ occurred.
At this point, sufficient circulation with the Atlantic Ocean was established that the deposition of Louann Salt ceased.
Seafloor spreading stopped at the end of the Jurassic, about 145–150 mya.

During the late Jurassic through early Cretaceous, the basin experienced a period of cooling and ___E:subsidence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidence)___ of the crust underlying it. The subsidence resulted from crustal stretching, cooling, and loading.
Initially, the crustal stretching and cooling combination caused about 5–7 km (3.1–4.3 miles) of tectonic subsidence of the central thin transitional and oceanic crust.

The basin expanded and deepened because subsidence occurred faster than sediment could fill it.    Later, loading of the crust within the basin and adjacent coastal plain by the accumulation of kilometers of sediments during the rest of the ___E:Mesozoic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesozoic)___ and all of the ___E:Cenozoic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cenozoic)___ further depressed the underlying crust to its current position about 10–20 km (6.2–12.4 miles) below sea level.

Particularly during the Cenozoic, a time of relative stability for the coastal zones,  thick ___E:clastic wedges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clastic_wedge)___ built out the continental shelf along the northwestern and northern margins of the basin.

To the east, the stable ___E:Florida Platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Platform)___ was not covered by the sea until the latest Jurassic or the beginning of Cretaceous time. The ___E:Yucatán Platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Platform)___ was emergent until the mid-Cretaceous.
After both platforms were submerged, the formation of ___E:carbonates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbonate_rock)___ and evaporites has delineated the geologic history of these two stable areas.

Most of the basin was rimmed during the early Cretaceous by carbonate platforms, and its western flank was involved during the latest Cretaceous and early ___E:Paleogene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleogene)___ periods in a compressive deformation episode, the ___E:Laramide Orogeny U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laramide_Orogeny)___ , which created the ___E:Sierra Madre Oriental U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Madre_Oriental)___ of eastern Mexico.

The Gulf of Mexico is 41% ___E:continental slope U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_margin)___ , 32% ___E:continental shelf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf)___ , and 24% ___E:abyssal plain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abyssal_plain)___ , with the greatest depth of 12,467 feet in the ___E:Sigsbee Deep U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigsbee_Deep)___ .
Seven main areas are given as: [citation needed]
A number of ___E:brine pools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brine_pool)___ , sometimes called brine lakes, are known on the seafloor of the northern half of the Gulf of Mexico.

Brine pools in the Gulf of Mexico range from just 1 metre (3 ft 3 in) across to 20 kilometres (12 mi) long. ___E:Brine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brine)___ is produced wherever the water of the Gulf comes in contact with the Louann Salt, an ___E:evaporite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaporite)___ formation from the Jurassic period, along faults or in unconsolidated sediments.
The Louann Salt extends under most of the continental shelf around the northern part of the Gulf from west of Florida to Texas.
Under the pressure of overlaying sediments, the salt deforms and migrates, a process known as ___E:salt tectonics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_tectonics)___ .

Masses of salt may rise through overlaying sediments to form ___E:salt domes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_domes)___ , or may be extruded along the ___E:Sigsbee Escarpment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigsbee_Escarpment)___ where the slope of the continental shelf exposes lower laying stata.
The brines usually exceed 200 ___E:parts-per-thousand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parts-per_notation)___ (ppt) of salt and are 25% or more denser than most seawater (average 35 ppt).
The density difference inhibits mixing of the brine with other sea water, and the brine flows downslope and gathers in depressions in the gulf floor.

Hydrocarbons and gas hydrates rising from salt ___E:diapirs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diapir)___ may cause doming of the gulf floor, with the gas sometimes erupting strongly enough to leave a depression in the gulf floor surrounded by a rim, where brine may pool. The East Flower Garden Bank brine pool is in a crater formed by the collapsed cap of a salt dome. The circular pool covers 500 square metres (5,400 sq ft) with a maximum depth of 25 centimetres (9.8 in), and is 70 metres (230 ft) beneath the surface of the Gulf. It is ___E:anoxic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anoxic_waters)___ and contain quantities of hydrogen sulfide and methane.  : 383
The brine pool known as GB425, which is 600 metres (2,000 ft) deep, is fed by a ___E:mud volcano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mud_volcano)___ .
The temperature at the surface of the pool can vary from 6 to 48 °C (43 to 118 °F), and is on average 20 °C (68 °F) warmer than normal bottom temperatures.
The brine pool known as GC233 is at a depth similar to that of GB425, 650 metres (2,130 ft) deep. The pool sits in a depression at the top of a mound and covers about 190 square metres (2,000 sq ft).

Although GC233 has a lower inflow of brine than GB425 and a temperature about 15 °C (59 °F) below that of GB425, the two pools share some similarities, such as a salinity of about 130 ppt, low sulfides, almost no sulfates, and high concentrations of hydrocarbons.
The ___E:Orca Basin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orca_Basin)___ is 2,100 metres (6,900 ft) deep, and covers about 400 square kilometres (150 sq mi) with a maximum depth of 350 metres (1,150 ft).
The large size is the result of the merger of several salt domes.
Salinity in the pool increases gradually over a depth of 75 metres (246 ft), and reaches 300 ppt at depth, with zero dissolved oxygen.  : 383–384

A brine pool was discovered in 2014 on the sea floor at a depth of 3,300 feet (1,000 m) with a circumference of 100 feet (30 m) and depth of 12 feet (4 m), which is four to five times saltier than the surrounding water.

The site cannot sustain any kind of life other than bacteria, ___E:mussels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mussel)___ with a ___E:symbiotic relationship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis)___ , ___E:tube worms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tube_worm)___ , and certain kinds of ___E:shrimp U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp)___ .
It has been called the "Jacuzzi of Despair" because it is warmer at 18 °C (65 °F) compared to the surrounding water at 4 °C (39 °F).
Circulation of water in and through the Gulf is part of the larger circulation patterns of the Atlantic Ocean.

Water flows into the Gulf from the Caribbean Sea through the ___E:Yucatan Channel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucatan_Channel)___ as the ___E:Yucatan Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucatan_Current)___ , and exits to the North Atlanic Ocean through the ___E:Florida Straits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Straits)___ as the ___E:Florida Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Current)___ , which becomes the ___E:Gulf Stream U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Stream)___ .

Movement through the two straits is confined to the upper layers of ocean water, as the Yucatan Strait has a maximum depth of only 1,800 metres (5,900 ft), while the Florida Straits has a maximum depth of only 900 metres (3,000 ft).  : 14221
The Yucatan Current fills most of the Yucatan Channel to a depth of up to 800 metres (2,600 ft), with a maximum flow of 120 centimetres (47 in) per second.
There are weaker countercurrents along the coasts of Cuba and Yucatan and below the main current.

The average ___E:volumetric flow rate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volumetric_flow_rate)___ through the Yucatan Channel varied between 15.8 and 28.1 ___E:Sverdrups U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sverdrup)___ ( ___E:hectometers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hectometers)___ per second) from 1999 to 2013. The Florida Current fills all of the Florida Straits (at approximately 81°W, between the lower ___E:Florida Keys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Keys)___ and Cuba) to a depth of 800 metres (2,600 ft), with a maximum flow of 110 centimetres (43 in) per second.
The average ___E:volumetric flow rate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volumetric_flow_rate)___ through the Florida Straits varied between 27.2 and 27.9 Sverdrups.  : 1382, 1388–1389

The Yucatan Current is connected to the Florida Current by an ___E:anti-cyclonic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclonic_rotation)___ (clockwise) loop of variable size, the ___E:Loop Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_Current)___ .
The Loop Current may extend into the northeastern part of the Gulf, and may flow over the continental shelf along the west coast of the Florida peninsula.

The Loop Current is as strong as the Gulf Stream and dominates the Gulf. Anti-cyclonic and cyclonic (anti-clockwise) rings or ___E:eddies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddy_(fluid_dynamics))___ are shed from the Loop Current and move into the western Gulf. Cyclonic and anti-cyclonic eddies form pairs, and such pairs of eddies often dominate circulation in the western Gulf.  : 14221  : 2
The Loop Current is up to 300 kilometres (190 mi) in diameter and is surrounded by small cyclonic (anti-clockwise) eddies.
Large warm-core rings or eddies are shed off the Loop Current at irregular intervals.

The Loop Current can be seen in satellite images using both ___E:sea surface temperatures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_surface_temperature)___ and ___E:Sea surface height U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_surface_topography)___ .  : 2 On the east side of the Gulf, a weak countercurrent flows north along the ___E:continental slope U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_margin)___ of the Florida peninsula.
In the Northeast corner of the Gulf there is a weak cyclonic circulation over the continental shelf.
The strength of this circulation is inversely proportional to how far north the Loop Current extends.  : 14234

The Loop Current is part of the ___E:North Atlantic Gyre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Gyre)___ , an ___E:ocean current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_current)___ circulation that includes the ___E:Gulf Stream U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Stream)___ , ___E:North Atlantic Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Current)___ , ___E:Canary Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canary_Current)___ , and ___E:North Equatorial Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Equatorial_Current)___ .

The eddies shed by the Loop Current spread though the Gulf, affecting the circulation in almost all parts of the Gulf. The creation of the eddies is a variable and often complex process, influenced in part by how far the Loop Currents has penetrated into the Gulf. Eddies shed by the Loop Current sometimes reattach to the Loop Current.
Eddies surrounding the Loop Current react interactively with it, affecting both the penetration of the loop into the Gulf, and the size and number of eddies shed by the loop.  : 13–14

Rings or eddies shed from the Loop Current may be up to 300 kilometres (190 mi) in diameter and 800 to 1,000 metres (2,600 to 3,300 ft) deep. The outer currents in the ring may flow at up to 4 knots (7.4 km/h; 4.6 mph), while the rings as a whole move westward at about 0.20 knots (0.37 km/h; 0.23 mph).  : 5
The water flowing into the Gulf from the Caribbean Sea is not homogenous.
About 40% is from the South Atlantic Ocean, and is warmer and fresher than the rest of the water.
The South Atlantic component is distinguishable in the upper 100 metres (330 ft) of the left hand and central parts of the Florida Current.
Another component in the deeper part of the current is ___E:Antarctic Intermediate Water U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctic_Intermediate_Water)___ .
The rest of the water carried into the Gulf consists of various masses from the North Atlantic.  : 15

As early as the ___E:Maya civilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_civilization)___ , the Gulf of Mexico was ___E:used as a trade route U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_trade_in_the_Maya_civilization)___ off the coast of the ___E:Yucatán Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Peninsula)___ and present-day ___E:Veracruz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veracruz)___ . [citation needed]

Although Europeans credited the Spanish voyage of ___E:Christopher Columbus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus)___ with the discovery of the Americas, the ships in his four voyages did not reach the Gulf of Mexico.
Instead, the Spanish sailed into the Caribbean around Cuba and ___E:Hispaniola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispaniola)___ .

The first alleged European exploration of the Gulf of Mexico was by ___E:Amerigo Vespucci U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amerigo_Vespucci)___ in 1497. Vespucci is purported to have followed the coastal land mass of Central America before returning to the Atlantic Ocean via the Straits of Florida between Florida and Cuba. However, this first voyage of 1497 is widely disputed.
Many historians doubt that it took place as described.

In his letters, Vespucci described this trip, and once ___E:Juan de la Cosa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_de_la_Cosa)___ returned to Spain, a ___E:famous world map U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Map_of_Juan_de_la_Cosa)___ was produced.

In 1506, ___E:Hernán Cortés U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Cort%C3%A9s)___ participated in the conquest of Hispaniola and Cuba, receiving a large estate of land and enslaving ___E:Indigenous U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas)___ people for his efforts.

In 1517, ___E:Francisco Hernández de Córdoba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Hern%C3%A1ndez_de_C%C3%B3rdoba_(Yucat%C3%A1n_conquistador))___ discovered the Yucatán Peninsula.

This was the first European encounter with an advanced civilization in the Americas, with solidly built buildings and complex social structures which they found comparable to those of the ___E:Old World U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_World)___ .

They also had reason to expect that this new land would have gold. All of this encouraged two further expeditions, the first in 1518 under the command of ___E:Juan de Grijalva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_de_Grijalva)___ , and the second in 1519 under the command of ___E:Hernán Cortés U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Cort%C3%A9s)___ , which led to the Spanish exploration, military invasion, and ultimately settlement and colonization known as the ___E:Conquest of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_conquest_of_the_Aztec_Empire)___ .

Hernández did not live to see the continuation of his work: he died in 1517, the year of his expedition, as the result of the injuries and the extreme thirst suffered during the voyage, and disappointed in the knowledge that Velázquez had given precedence to Grijalva as the captain of the next expedition to Yucatán.
In 1523, a ___E:treasure ship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_treasure_fleet)___ was wrecked en route at ___E:Padre Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padre_Island)___ , Texas.

When word of the disaster reached Mexico City, the viceroy requested a rescue fleet and sent ___E:Ángel de Villafañe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_de_Villafa%C3%B1e)___ from Mexico City, marching overland to find the treasure-laden vessels.

This loss, combined with other ship disasters around the Gulf of Mexico, led to a plan for establishing a settlement on the northern Gulf Coast to protect shipping and rescue castaways more quickly.

As a result, the expedition of ___E:Tristán de Luna y Arellano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trist%C3%A1n_de_Luna_y_Arellano)___ was sent and landed at ___E:Pensacola Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_Bay)___ on August 15, 1559.

On December 11, 1526, ___E:Charles V U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor)___ of the ___E:Holy Roman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire)___ granted ___E:Pánfilo de Narváez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C3%A1nfilo_de_Narv%C3%A1ez)___ a license to establish colonial settlements along the present-day Gulf Coast of the United States, known as the ___E:Narváez expedition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narv%C3%A1ez_expedition)___ .
The contract gave him one year to gather an army, leave Spain, be large enough to found at least two towns of 100 people each, and garrison two more fortresses anywhere along the coast.
On April 7, 1528, they spotted land north of what is now ___E:Tampa Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay)___ .

In 1697, French sailor ___E:Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Moyne_d%27Iberville)___ was chosen by the Minister of Marine to lead an expedition to rediscover the mouth of the ___E:Mississippi River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River)___ and to settle ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ , which French explorer ___E:Robert Cavelier de La Salle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Cavelier_de_La_Salle)___ had named.

The first permanent settlement, Fort Maurepas (now ___E:Ocean Springs, Mississippi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Springs,_Mississippi)___ ), was founded in 1699 by d'Iberville.

By then the French had also built a small fort at the mouth of the Mississippi at a settlement they named ___E:La Balize (or La Balize) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Balize,_Louisiana)___ , " ___E:seamark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_mark)___ " in French.
The Gulf of Mexico's eastern, northern, and northwestern shores lie along the US states of Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Texas.

The US portion of the coastline spans 2,700 km (1,700 miles),  receiving water from 33 major rivers that drain 31 states and 2 Canadian provinces, and consisting of the coastline from the southern tip of Florida and the ___E:Florida Keys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Keys)___ to the ___E:U.S.–Mexican border U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S.%E2%80%93Mexican_border)___ between ___E:Brownsville, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas)___ , and ___E:Matamoros, Tamaulipas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matamoros,_Tamaulipas)___ .

The Mexican coastline spans 2,200 km (1,400 miles), consisting of the coastline from the US border to the ___E:Cabo Catoche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabo_Catoche)___ ___E:Light U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_lighthouses_in_Mexico)___ (near ___E:Cancún U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canc%C3%BAn)___ ) at the northern tip of the ___E:Yucatán Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Peninsula)___ .

Cuba has only 100–400 km (60–250 miles) of official gulf coastline, along its northern land boundary.   [dubious – discuss] The southwestern and southern shores of the gulf lie along the ___E:Mexican states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_of_Mexico)___ of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche, Yucatán, and the northernmost tip of Quintana Roo. On its southeast quadrant, the gulf is bordered by Cuba. It supports major American, Mexican, and Cuban fishing industries.

The outer margins of the wide continental shelves of Yucatán and Florida receive cooler, nutrient-enriched waters from the deep by a process known as ___E:upweling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Upweling&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , which stimulates plankton growth in the ___E:euphotic zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photic_zone)___ .
This attracts fish, shrimp, and squid.
River drainage and atmospheric fallout from industrial coastal cities also provide nutrients to the coastal zone.

The ___E:Gulf Stream U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Stream)___ , a warm Atlantic Ocean current and one of the strongest ___E:ocean currents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_current)___ known, originates in the gulf as a continuation of the ___E:Caribbean Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Current)___ –Yucatán Current– ___E:Loop Current U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_Current)___ system.

Other circulation features include a permanent cyclonic ___E:gyre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_gyre)___ in the ___E:Bay of Campeche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Campeche)___ and anticyclonic gyres, which are shed by the Loop Current and travel westwards, where they eventually dissipate.
The Bay of Campeche constitutes a major arm of the Gulf of Mexico.
Numerous bays and smaller inlets fringe the gulf's shoreline.

Streams that empty into the gulf include the Mississippi River and the Rio Grande in the northern gulf and the ___E:Grijalva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grijalva_River)___ and ___E:Usumacinta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usumacinta_River)___ rivers in the southern gulf. The land that forms the gulf's coast, including many long, narrow barrier islands, is almost uniformly low-lying and is defined by marshes, swamps, and stretches of sandy beach.
The Gulf of Mexico is an excellent example of a ___E:passive margin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_margin)___ .
The ___E:continental shelf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf)___ is quite wide at most points along the coast, notably at the Florida and Yucatán Peninsulas.
The shelf is exploited for its ___E:oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum)___ through offshore drilling rigs, most of which are situated in the western gulf and the Bay of Campeche.

Another important commercial activity is fishing; major catches include ___E:red snapper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_red_snapper)___ , ___E:amberjack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amberjack)___ , ___E:tilefish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilefish)___ , ___E:swordfish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swordfish)___ , and various ___E:grouper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grouper)___ , as well as ___E:shrimp U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp)___ and crabs. ___E:Oysters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oysters)___ are also harvested on a large scale from many bays and sounds.
Other important industries along the coast include shipping, petrochemical processing and storage, military use, paper manufacture, and tourism.

The gulf is considered ___E:aseismic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aseismic)___ ; however, mild tremors have been recorded throughout history (usually 5.0 or less on the ___E:Richter magnitude scale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richter_magnitude_scale)___ ).
Interactions between sediment loading on the sea floor and adjustment by the crust may cause earthquakes.

On September 10, 2006, the ___E:U.S. Geological Survey National Earthquake Information Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey)___ reported that a ___E:magnitude 6.0 earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Gulf_of_Mexico_earthquake)___ occurred about 400 km (250 miles) west-southwest of ___E:Anna Maria, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Maria,_Florida)___ .
The quake was reportedly felt from Louisiana to Florida.
There were no reports of damage or injuries.
Items were knocked from shelves and ___E:seiches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seiche)___ were observed in swimming pools in parts of Florida.

The earthquake was described by the ___E:USGS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USGS)___ as an ___E:intraplate earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intraplate_earthquake)___ , the largest and most widely felt recorded in the past three decades in the region.

According to The Tampa Tribune on the following day, earthquake tremors were last felt in Florida in 1952, recorded in ___E:Quincy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy,_Florida)___ , 32 km (20 miles) northwest of ___E:Tallahassee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallahassee,_Florida)___ .

Cuba and Mexico : Exchange of notes constituting an agreement on the ___E:delimitation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_boundary_delimitation)___ of the exclusive economic zone of Mexico in the sector adjacent to Cuban maritime areas (with map), of July 1976.
Cuba and United States : ___E:Maritime boundary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_boundary)___ agreement between the United States of America and the Republic of Cuba, of December 1977.

Mexico and United States : Treaty to resolve pending boundary differences and maintain the Rio Grande and Colorado River as the international boundary, of November 1970; Treaty on maritime boundaries between the United States of America and the United Mexican States (Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean), of May 1978, and treaty on the delimitation of the continental shelf in the western Gulf of Mexico beyond 200 ___E:nautical miles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile)___ (370 km; 230 mi), of June 2000.
In December 2007, Mexico submitted information to the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) regarding the extension of Mexico's continental shelf beyond 200 nautical miles.

Mexico sought an extension of its continental shelf in the Western Polygon based on international law, UNCLOS, and bilateral treaties with the United States, in accordance with Mexico's domestic legislation.
In March 2009, the CLCS accepted Mexico's arguments for extending its continental shelf up to 350 nautical miles (650 km; 400 mi) into the Western Polygon.

Since this would extend Mexico's continental shelf well into territory claimed by the United States, Mexico and the United States would need to enter a bilateral agreement based on international law that delimits their respective claims.
A ship now called the Mardi Gras sank around the early 19th century about 56 km (35 mi) off the coast of Louisiana in 1,200 m (3,900 feet) of water.
The ship, whose real identity remains a mystery, is believed to have been a ___E:privateer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privateer)___ or trader.
The shipwreck lay forgotten at the bottom of the sea until it was discovered in 2002 by an oilfield inspection crew working for the Okeanos Gas Gathering Company (OGGC).

In 2007, an expedition led by Texas A&M University and funded by OGGC under an agreement with the Minerals Management Service (now ___E:BOEM U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BOEM)___ ) was launched to undertake the deepest scientific archaeological excavation to that date to study the site on the seafloor and recover artifacts for public display in the ___E:Louisiana State Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Museum)___ .

Video footage from the ROV was used in the documentary.

On July 30, 1942, the ___E:SS Robert E. Lee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Robert_E._Lee)___ , captained by William C. Heath, was torpedoed by the ___E:German submarine U-166 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-166_(1941))___ .

The steamship was en route to ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ , sailing southeast of the entrance to the Mississippi River; she was being escorted by USS PC-566 , captained by Lieutenant Commander Herbert G. Claudius.

The explosion destroyed the No. 3 hold; vented through the B and C decks; and damaged the engines, the radio compartment, and the steering gear. PC-566 dropped ___E:depth charges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge)___ on a ___E:sonar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonar)___ contact, sinking U-166 .
The badly damaged Robert E. Lee first listed to port, then to starboard, and finally sank within about 15 minutes of the attack.
One officer, nine crew members, and 15 passengers were lost. The passengers aboard Robert E. Lee were primarily survivors of previous torpedo attacks by German U-boats.
In 2001, the wrecks of U-166 and Robert E. Lee were found during the C & C Marine survey.
The submarine was found in 5,000 feet (1,500 m) of water, about three km (1.9 miles) from where it had attacked the liner.

Various biota include ___E:chemosynthetic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemosynthesis)___ communities near ___E:cold seeps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_seep)___ and nonchemosynthetic communities such as bacteria and other micro- ___E:benthos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benthos)___ , ___E:meiofauna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiofauna)___ , ___E:macrofauna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macrofauna)___ , and ___E:megafauna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megafauna)___ (larger organisms such as crabs, ___E:sea pens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_pen)___ , ___E:crinoids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crinoid)___ , ___E:demersal fish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demersal_fish)___ , ___E:cetaceans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetacean)___ , and the extinct ___E:Caribbean monk seal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_monk_seal)___ ) are living in the Gulf of Mexico.

Recently, resident ___E:Bryde's whales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryde%27s_whale)___ within the gulf were classified as an endemic, unique subspecies and making them as one of the most endangered whales in the world.

The Gulf of Mexico yields more fish, shrimp, and shellfish annually than the south and ___E:mid-Atlantic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Atlantic_states)___ , ___E:Chesapeake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay)___ , and ___E:New England U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England)___ areas combined.

The ___E:Smithsonian Institution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Institution)___ Gulf of Mexico holdings are expected to provide an important baseline of understanding for future scientific studies on the impact of the ___E:Deepwater Horizon oil spill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon_oil_spill)___ .

In Congressional testimony, ___E:Jonathan Coddington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Coddington)___ , associate director of Research and Collections at the Smithsonian's ___E:National Museum of Natural History U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Natural_History)___ , provides a detailed overview of the Gulf collections and their sources which Museum staff have made available on an online map. The samples were collected for years by the former Minerals Management Service (renamed the ___E:Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, Regulation and Enforcement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Ocean_Energy_Management,_Regulation_and_Enforcement)___ ) to help predict the potential impacts of future oil/gas explorations.
Since 1979, the specimens have been deposited in the national collections of the National Museum of Natural History.

The major environmental threats to the gulf are ___E:agricultural runoff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_pollution)___ and ___E:oil drilling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_drilling)___ .
There are 27,000 abandoned oil and gas wells beneath the gulf. These have generally not been checked for potential environmental problems.

In 1973 the ___E:United States Environmental Protection Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency)___ prohibited the dumping of undiluted chemical waste by manufacturing sediment interests into the gulf, and the military confessed to similar behavior in waters off ___E:Horn Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_Island_(Mississippi))___ .  ___E:Microplastics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microplastics)___ within semi-enclosed seas like the gulf have been reported in high concentrations and the gulf's first such study estimated concentrations that rival the highest globally reported.

There are frequent " ___E:red tide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algal_bloom#Red_tides)___ " algae blooms  that kill fish and marine mammals and cause respiratory problems in humans and some domestic animals when the blooms reach close to shore.

This has especially been plaguing the southwest and southern Florida coast, from the ___E:Florida Keys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Keys)___ to north of ___E:Pasco County, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasco_County,_Florida)___ .

The gulf contains a ___E:hypoxic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoxia_(environmental))___ ___E:dead zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_zone_(ecology))___ that runs east–west along the Texas–Louisiana coastline.
In July 2008, researchers reported that between 1985 and 2008, the area roughly doubled in size.  It was 22,730 km 2 (8,780 square miles) in 2017, the largest ever recorded.

Poor agricultural practices in the northern portion of the Gulf of Mexico have led to a tremendous increase of ___E:nitrogen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen)___ and ___E:phosphorus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphorus)___ in neighboring marine ecosystems, which has resulted in ___E:algae U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae)___ blooms and a lack of available oxygen.
Occurrences of ___E:virilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virilization)___ and ___E:estrogen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estrogen)___ suppression were observed as a result.
A 2007 study of the ___E:Atlantic croaker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_croaker)___ found a disproportioned sex ratio of 61% males to 39% females in hypoxic sites.
This was compared with a 52% to 48% male-female ratio found in reference sites, showing impaired reproductive output for fish populations inhabiting hypoxic coastal zones.
According to the ___E:National Response Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Response_Center)___ , the oil industry has thousands of minor accidents annually in the Gulf of Mexico.

The gulf's largest ___E:oil spill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixtoc_I_oil_spill)___ to date began in June 1979, when the Ixtoc I ___E:oil platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_platform)___ in the Bay of Campeche suffered a ___E:blowout U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blowout_(well_drilling))___ and a catastrophic explosion, and lasted until the well was finally capped in April 1980.

On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon oil platform, located in the ___E:Mississippi Canyon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Canyon)___ about 64 km (40 miles) off the Louisiana coast and operated by the British multinational company ___E:BP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BP)___ , ___E:suffered a catastrophic explosion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon_explosion)___ and later sank.   [d] Oil flowed from the ___E:wellhead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellhead)___ , about 1.5 km (0.9 mi) below the surface on the ocean floor,  creating a ___E:slick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_spill)___ that covered hundreds of square kilometers of ocean surface, threatening marine life, adjacent ___E:coastal wetlands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_marsh)___ , and the livelihoods of Gulf Coast shrimpers and fishermen.

Estimates of the daily flow jumped several times—on April 24, it was 160 cubic metres (1,000 bbl) by BP's estimate; on April 28, a ___E:NOAA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOAA)___ scientist increased the estimate to 5,000 barrels (790 m 3 );   and on May 27 the ___E:USGS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USGS)___ put the rate at 12,000–19,000 barrels per day (1,900–3,000 m 3 /d).

Final estimates suggested a leak of 62,000 barrels per day (9,900 m 3 /d), a scale that had been suggested by both independent observers and federal scientists early on, but official attempts to release modeling data had been suppressed by the ___E:White House Office of Management and Budget U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Office_of_Management_and_Budget)___ according to a report by ___E:the government commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Commission_on_the_BP_Deepwater_Horizon_Oil_Spill_and_Offshore_Drilling)___ investigating the response.   : 10 On July 15, BP announced that the leak had stopped.
In July, BP agreed to pay $18.7 billion to the U.S. government, the states of Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Texas, as well as 400 local authorities.
As of 2015 [update] , BP had spent $54 billion on cleanup, penalties, and to repair environmental and economic damage.

On May 12, 2016, oil from subsea infrastructure on ___E:Shell's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dutch_Shell)___ Brutus oil rig released 2,100 barrels of oil. This leak created a 5 to 34 km (3.1 to 21.1 mi) oil slick in the sea about 156 km (97 miles) south of ___E:Port Fourchon, Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Fourchon,_Louisiana)___ , according to the U.S.
Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement.

The gulf's warm ___E:sea surface temperatures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_surface_temperature)___ can feed powerful, deadly, and destructive ___E:Atlantic hurricanes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_hurricane)___ such as ___E:Hurricane Katrina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina)___ in ___E:2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Atlantic_hurricane_season)___ .

In the open Atlantic, a ___E:hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone)___ will ___E:draw up U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upwelling)___ cool water from the depths, making it less likely that further hurricanes will follow (warm water being one of the preconditions necessary for their formation).
However, the gulf is shallower; when a hurricane passes over, the water temperature may drop, but it soon rebounds enough to support another tropical cyclone.
From 1970 to 2020, surface temperatures warmed at about twice the rate observed for the global ocean surface.

Moisture from the Gulf of Mexico is a primary factor for the development of tornadoes and other severe weather in ___E:Tornado Alley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_Alley)___ , a term used to describe an area of the United States that is one of the most tornado-prone areas in the world.

Dry air from the ___E:Rocky Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains)___ converges with Gulf moisture in the area, which produces storms and ___E:supercells U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercell)___ that produce some of the most violent tornadoes in the world.

A study published in the Journal of Climate by Dongmin Kim, Sang-Ki Lee, and Hosmay Lopez, found that the ___E:Madden–Julian oscillation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madden%E2%80%93Julian_oscillation)___ strengthens the North American low-level jet, which increases the flow of Gulf moisture and ___E:atmospheric instability U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_instability)___ into the Central United States, furthering ___E:tornadogenesis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornadogenesis)___ in the region.
